### <a id="html-a11y-0009"></a> HTML-A11Y-0009 — Do not use positive tabindex values.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Accessibility → A11Y → Accessibility → HTML-A11Y-0009`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Accessibility`

Do not use positive tabindex values.

Rationale: Positive tabindex creates a custom focus order that quickly diverges from visual and DOM order.

**Example / guidance:**

```text
Use natural order or tabindex="0" / "-1" when genuinely required.
```

**Rationale:** Positive tabindex creates a custom focus order that quickly diverges from visual and DOM order.

**Validation:** Run HTML validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="html-a11y-0010"></a> HTML-A11Y-0010 — Keep DOM order consistent with meaningful reading and focus order.

**Priority:** `MUST`

**Applicability:** `Browser && Accessibility`

Keep DOM order consistent with meaningful reading and focus order.

Rationale: CSS visual reordering must not create a different logical sequence for keyboard or assistive-technology users.

**Example / guidance:**

```text

```

**Rationale:** CSS visual reordering must not create a different logical sequence for keyboard or assistive-technology users.

**Validation:** Run HTML validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

### <a id="html-a11y-0011"></a> HTML-A11Y-0011 — Expose dynamic status changes through an appropriate live region when necessary.

**Rationale:** Important asynchronous updates may otherwise be invisible to screen-reader users.

### <a id="html-perf-0001"></a> HTML-PERF-0001 — Keep the initial DOM proportional to visible and immediately interactive content.

### <a id="html-perf-0002"></a> HTML-PERF-0002 — Load scripts with module semantics when using modern JavaScript.

**Priority:** `MUST`

**Applicability:** `Browser && Performance & Loading`

Load scripts with module semantics when using modern JavaScript.

**Rationale:** type="module" is deferred by default and establishes explicit module loading.

**Rationale:** Synchronous classic scripts delay HTML parsing unless intentionally required.

### <a id="html-perf-0004"></a> HTML-PERF-0004 — Preload only resources that are definitely needed early.

## Glossary

- **MUST:** Mandatory requirement unless an explicit, justified exception is recorded.
- **SHOULD:** Strong recommendation; deviations require a concrete reason.
- **MAY:** Optional guidance whose applicability depends on context.
- **applicability:** The environments, runtimes, APIs, and scopes in which a rule is relevant.
- **autofix:** Whether a rule can be safely transformed automatically.
- **knowledge graph:** Rules plus inheritance bases and explicit typed relations.

## Rules by Category

### General / GEN

| Rule | Priority | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `CSS-GEN-0001` | MUST | Keep CSS in external stylesheet files. |
| `CSS-GEN-0002` | MUST | Use modern CSS directly when project browser support permits it. |
| `CSS-GEN-0003` | MUST | Prefer declarative CSS over JavaScript-driven presentation. |
| `CSS-GEN-0004` | SHOULD | Use a deterministic formatter and consistent property ordering. |
| `CSS-GEN-0005` | MUST | Remove dead declarations and selectors. |
| `CSS-GEN-0006` | MUST | Avoid !important. |
| `CSS-GEN-0007` | SHOULD | Prefer logical properties when layout should adapt to writing mode. |
| `CSS-GEN-0008` | SHOULD | Use comments for non-obvious constraints and public styling APIs. |
| `CSS-GEN-0009` | MUST | Do not create one-use custom properties that add indirection without semantic value. |
| `CSS-GEN-0010` | MUST | Keep source order intentional. |

### Cascade & Specificity / CAS

| Rule | Priority | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `CSS-CAS-0001` | MUST | Use cascade layers to express stylesheet precedence when multiple origins of project CSS compete. |
| `CSS-CAS-0002` | MUST | Keep component selectors low-specificity. |
| `CSS-CAS-0003` | MUST | Avoid id selectors for styling. |
| `CSS-CAS-0004` | MUST | Avoid specificity escalation as an override strategy. |
| `CSS-CAS-0005` | MUST | Use :where() when a selector should contribute zero specificity. |
| `CSS-CAS-0006` | SHOULD | Use :is() to group equivalent selector branches without duplication. |
| `CSS-CAS-0007` | MUST | Keep state selectors adjacent to the component rules they modify. |
| `CSS-CAS-0008` | MUST | Do not rely on accidental stylesheet import order. |
| `CSS-CAS-0009` | MUST | Prefer custom properties over repeated override selectors for configurable values. |
| `CSS-CAS-0010` | MUST | Scope exceptions narrowly. |

### Selectors & Naming / SEL

| Rule | Priority | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `CSS-SEL-0001` | MUST | Name classes by semantic role or component responsibility. |
| `CSS-SEL-0002` | MUST | Use classes as the default styling hook. |
| `CSS-SEL-0003` | MUST | Avoid styling behavior-only data attributes unless the state itself is part of the styling API. |
| `CSS-SEL-0004` | MUST | Avoid deep descendant selectors. |
| `CSS-SEL-0005` | MUST | Prefer direct child selectors when component structure is contractual. |
| `CSS-SEL-0006` | MUST | Use attribute selectors for actual attribute semantics. |
| `CSS-SEL-0007` | MUST | Use pseudo-classes for interaction and structural states before extra classes. |
| `CSS-SEL-0008` | MUST | Use :has() only when the relationship itself is the styling condition. |
| `CSS-SEL-0009` | MUST | Avoid universal-selector rules outside deliberate resets or scoped algorithms. |
| `CSS-SEL-0010` | MUST | Keep selector lists semantically homogeneous. |

### Custom Properties & Tokens / TOK

| Rule | Priority | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `CSS-TOK-0001` | MUST | Represent shared design decisions as custom properties. |
| `CSS-TOK-0002` | MUST | Name tokens by purpose before raw appearance. |
| `CSS-TOK-0003` | MUST | Separate global design tokens from component-local variables. |
| `CSS-TOK-0004` | MUST | Provide defaults for externally overridable component custom properties when sensible. |
| `CSS-TOK-0005` | MUST | Avoid mirroring every declaration into a custom property. |
| `CSS-TOK-0006` | SHOULD | Use typed @property registration only when its behavior is required. |
| `CSS-TOK-0007` | MUST | Keep token units semantically appropriate. |
| `CSS-TOK-0008` | MUST | Derive related values with calc(), min(), max(), clamp(), and color functions instead of duplicating constants. |
| `CSS-TOK-0009` | SHOULD | Use color-mix() when a color is semantically derived from another token. |
| `CSS-TOK-0010` | SHOULD | Document public custom properties at the component boundary. |

### Layout / LAY

| Rule | Priority | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `CSS-LAY-0001` | MUST | Use Grid for two-dimensional layout and Flexbox for one-dimensional distribution when they fit the problem. |
| `CSS-LAY-0002` | MUST | Avoid absolute positioning for primary document layout. |
| `CSS-LAY-0003` | MUST | Use gap for spacing between grid/flex items. |
| `CSS-LAY-0004` | MUST | Prefer intrinsic sizing before hard-coded dimensions. |
| `CSS-LAY-0005` | MUST | Use minmax(0, 1fr) or min-width: 0 where overflow semantics require flexible tracks to shrink. |
| `CSS-LAY-0006` | MUST | Avoid fixed heights for text-driven containers. |
| `CSS-LAY-0007` | MUST | Use aspect-ratio for proportional boxes. |
| `CSS-LAY-0008` | MUST | Use position: sticky only within a clearly understood scroll container. |
| `CSS-LAY-0009` | MUST | Keep z-index within explicit stacking-context ownership. |
| `CSS-LAY-0010` | MUST | Create containing blocks intentionally. |
| `CSS-LAY-0011` | SHOULD | Use subgrid when descendants must align to an ancestor grid and support is within target browsers. |

### Responsive & Container Design / RESP

| Rule | Priority | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `CSS-RESP-0001` | MUST | Prefer container queries for component-local responsiveness. |
| `CSS-RESP-0002` | MUST | Use media queries for environment or viewport-level conditions. |
| `CSS-RESP-0003` | MUST | Choose breakpoints from content behavior, not device names. |
| `CSS-RESP-0004` | MUST | Use clamp() for bounded fluid values when continuous scaling is appropriate. |
| `CSS-RESP-0005` | MUST | Do not duplicate complete component trees for responsive layouts. |
| `CSS-RESP-0006` | MUST | Test narrow containers independently of narrow viewports. |
| `CSS-RESP-0007` | MUST | Use dynamic viewport units deliberately. |
| `CSS-RESP-0008` | MUST | Respect safe-area insets only where edge-to-edge layouts require them. |
| `CSS-RESP-0009` | MUST | Avoid orientation queries when available space can express the requirement better. |
| `CSS-RESP-0010` | MUST | Keep responsive overrides close to the component when project architecture permits it. |

### Typography & Content / TYPE

| Rule | Priority | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `CSS-TYPE-0001` | MUST | Use relative units for user-scalable text. |
| `CSS-TYPE-0002` | MUST | Define line-height without unnecessary units for normal text. |
| `CSS-TYPE-0003` | MUST | Do not truncate important content without an accessible way to obtain it. |
| `CSS-TYPE-0004` | MUST | Use text-wrap and overflow-wrap primitives before manual line-break markup. |
| `CSS-TYPE-0005` | MUST | Avoid disabling text selection on ordinary content. |
| `CSS-TYPE-0006` | MUST | Keep font fallback stacks compatible with intended metrics and script coverage. |
| `CSS-TYPE-0007` | MUST | Use font-display deliberately for web fonts. |
| `CSS-TYPE-0008` | SHOULD | Subset or preload fonts only from measured requirements. |
| `CSS-TYPE-0009` | MUST | Use ch only when character-based sizing matches the design intent. |
| `CSS-TYPE-0010` | MUST | Allow text to reflow at increased zoom and text size. |

### Interaction & Animation / MOTION

| Rule | Priority | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `CSS-MOTION-0001` | MUST | Animate transform and opacity when they can express the effect. |
| `CSS-MOTION-0002` | MUST | Avoid animating layout properties in high-frequency effects. |
| `CSS-MOTION-0003` | MUST | Respect prefers-reduced-motion. |
| `CSS-MOTION-0004` | MUST | Keep transition-property explicit. |
| `CSS-MOTION-0005` | MUST | Use durations and easing as semantic tokens when repeated. |
| `CSS-MOTION-0006` | MUST | Do not use hover as the only way to expose required information or controls. |
| `CSS-MOTION-0007` | MUST | Style :focus-visible explicitly. |
| `CSS-MOTION-0008` | MUST | Do not remove outlines without providing an equal or stronger focus indicator. |
| `CSS-MOTION-0009` | MUST | Use pointer coarse/hover media features only for capability adaptation, not device guessing. |
| `CSS-MOTION-0010` | SHOULD | Avoid infinite animation unless it communicates active state or is intentionally decorative and inexpensive. |

### Accessibility / A11Y

| Rule | Priority | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `CSS-A11Y-0001` | MUST | Maintain sufficient text and UI contrast. |
| `CSS-A11Y-0002` | MUST | Do not communicate state by color alone. |
| `CSS-A11Y-0003` | MUST | Preserve visible keyboard focus. |
| `CSS-A11Y-0004` | MUST | Respect forced-colors mode when custom styling would obscure controls. |
| `CSS-A11Y-0005` | MUST | Do not disable browser zoom through CSS/viewport-related assumptions. |
| `CSS-A11Y-0006` | SHOULD | Ensure interactive target sizing remains usable. |
| `CSS-A11Y-0007` | MUST | Avoid content insertion with CSS when the content is semantically meaningful. |
| `CSS-A11Y-0008` | MUST | Do not reorder meaningful content solely with flex/grid order. |
| `CSS-A11Y-0009` | MUST | Support user color-scheme preferences only when both themes are complete. |
| `CSS-A11Y-0010` | SHOULD | Use motion, transparency, and contrast preferences as progressive user adaptations. |

### Performance & Rendering / PERF

| Rule | Priority | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `CSS-PERF-0001` | MUST | Measure before applying performance-specific CSS complexity. |
| `CSS-PERF-0002` | MUST | Avoid selectors and rules that cause broad unnecessary invalidation in frequently mutating regions. |
| `CSS-PERF-0003` | MUST | Use contain when isolation semantics are correct. |
| `CSS-PERF-0004` | SHOULD | Use content-visibility for large offscreen sections only when its accessibility and sizing behavior is understood. |
| `CSS-PERF-0005` | MUST | Avoid excessive box-shadow, filter, backdrop-filter, and large blur effects in animated surfaces. |
| `CSS-PERF-0006` | MUST | Do not add will-change permanently to many elements. |
| `CSS-PERF-0007` | MUST | Minimize layout thrash by keeping measurement/mutation sequencing in JavaScript rather than trying to compensate with CSS hacks. |
| `CSS-PERF-0008` | MUST | Reduce unused CSS delivered on critical routes. |
| `CSS-PERF-0009` | MUST | Prefer one coherent rule over many mutually overriding declarations. |
| `CSS-PERF-0010` | SHOULD | Treat expensive visual effects as responsive to device/user capability where appropriate. |

### Compatibility & Quality / QUAL

| Rule | Priority | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `CSS-QUAL-0001` | MUST | Run a CSS linter in CI. |
| `CSS-QUAL-0002` | MUST | Test supported browser engines rather than relying on syntax compilation alone. |
| `CSS-QUAL-0003` | MUST | Use feature queries for optional enhancements when support varies across targets. |
| `CSS-QUAL-0004` | MUST | Avoid browser-targeted hacks unless a documented engine bug requires them. |
| `CSS-QUAL-0005` | SHOULD | Document compatibility workarounds with bug/reference and removal criteria. |
| `CSS-QUAL-0006` | MUST | Keep source maps and generated CSS out of handwritten source ownership. |
| `CSS-QUAL-0007` | MUST | Test themes, interaction states, long content, empty content, and zoom. |
| `CSS-QUAL-0008` | SHOULD | Use visual regression tests for high-value stable components where practical. |
| `CSS-QUAL-0009` | MUST | Review computed styles when debugging rather than adding speculative overrides. |
| `CSS-QUAL-0010` | MUST | Delete superseded compatibility rules promptly. |

- [`CSS-TYPE-0002`](#css-type-0002) — Define line-height without unnecessary units for normal text.
- [`CSS-TYPE-0003`](#css-type-0003) — Do not truncate important content without an accessible way to obtain it.
- [`CSS-TYPE-0004`](#css-type-0004) — Use text-wrap and overflow-wrap primitives before manual line-break markup.
- [`CSS-TYPE-0005`](#css-type-0005) — Avoid disabling text selection on ordinary content.
- [`CSS-TYPE-0006`](#css-type-0006) — Keep font fallback stacks compatible with intended metrics and script coverage.
- [`CSS-TYPE-0007`](#css-type-0007) — Use font-display deliberately for web fonts.
- [`CSS-TYPE-0008`](#css-type-0008) — Subset or preload fonts only from measured requirements.
- [`CSS-TYPE-0009`](#css-type-0009) — Use ch only when character-based sizing matches the design intent.
- [`CSS-TYPE-0010`](#css-type-0010) — Allow text to reflow at increased zoom and text size.
- [`CSS-MOTION-0001`](#css-motion-0001) — Animate transform and opacity when they can express the effect.
- [`CSS-MOTION-0002`](#css-motion-0002) — Avoid animating layout properties in high-frequency effects.
- [`CSS-MOTION-0003`](#css-motion-0003) — Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
- [`CSS-MOTION-0004`](#css-motion-0004) — Keep transition-property explicit.
- [`CSS-MOTION-0005`](#css-motion-0005) — Use durations and easing as semantic tokens when repeated.
- [`CSS-MOTION-0006`](#css-motion-0006) — Do not use hover as the only way to expose required information or controls.
- [`CSS-MOTION-0007`](#css-motion-0007) — Style :focus-visible explicitly.
- [`CSS-MOTION-0008`](#css-motion-0008) — Do not remove outlines without providing an equal or stronger focus indicator.
- [`CSS-MOTION-0009`](#css-motion-0009) — Use pointer coarse/hover media features only for capability adaptation, not device guessing.
- [`CSS-MOTION-0010`](#css-motion-0010) — Avoid infinite animation unless it communicates active state or is intentionally decorative and inexpensive.
- [`CSS-A11Y-0001`](#css-a11y-0001) — Maintain sufficient text and UI contrast.
- [`CSS-A11Y-0002`](#css-a11y-0002) — Do not communicate state by color alone.
- [`CSS-A11Y-0003`](#css-a11y-0003) — Preserve visible keyboard focus.
- [`CSS-A11Y-0004`](#css-a11y-0004) — Respect forced-colors mode when custom styling would obscure controls.
- [`CSS-A11Y-0005`](#css-a11y-0005) — Do not disable browser zoom through CSS/viewport-related assumptions.
- [`CSS-A11Y-0006`](#css-a11y-0006) — Ensure interactive target sizing remains usable.
- [`CSS-A11Y-0007`](#css-a11y-0007) — Avoid content insertion with CSS when the content is semantically meaningful.
- [`CSS-A11Y-0008`](#css-a11y-0008) — Do not reorder meaningful content solely with flex/grid order.
- [`CSS-A11Y-0009`](#css-a11y-0009) — Support user color-scheme preferences only when both themes are complete.
- [`CSS-A11Y-0010`](#css-a11y-0010) — Use motion, transparency, and contrast preferences as progressive user adaptations.
- [`CSS-PERF-0001`](#css-perf-0001) — Measure before applying performance-specific CSS complexity.
- [`CSS-PERF-0002`](#css-perf-0002) — Avoid selectors and rules that cause broad unnecessary invalidation in frequently mutating regions.
- [`CSS-PERF-0003`](#css-perf-0003) — Use contain when isolation semantics are correct.
- [`CSS-PERF-0004`](#css-perf-0004) — Use content-visibility for large offscreen sections only when its accessibility and sizing behavior is understood.
- [`CSS-PERF-0005`](#css-perf-0005) — Avoid excessive box-shadow, filter, backdrop-filter, and large blur effects in animated surfaces.
- [`CSS-PERF-0006`](#css-perf-0006) — Do not add will-change permanently to many elements.
- [`CSS-PERF-0007`](#css-perf-0007) — Minimize layout thrash by keeping measurement/mutation sequencing in JavaScript rather than trying to compensate with CSS hacks.
- [`CSS-PERF-0008`](#css-perf-0008) — Reduce unused CSS delivered on critical routes.
- [`CSS-PERF-0009`](#css-perf-0009) — Prefer one coherent rule over many mutually overriding declarations.
- [`CSS-PERF-0010`](#css-perf-0010) — Treat expensive visual effects as responsive to device/user capability where appropriate.
- [`CSS-QUAL-0001`](#css-qual-0001) — Run a CSS linter in CI.
- [`CSS-QUAL-0002`](#css-qual-0002) — Test supported browser engines rather than relying on syntax compilation alone.
- [`CSS-QUAL-0003`](#css-qual-0003) — Use feature queries for optional enhancements when support varies across targets.
- [`CSS-QUAL-0004`](#css-qual-0004) — Avoid browser-targeted hacks unless a documented engine bug requires them.
- [`CSS-QUAL-0005`](#css-qual-0005) — Document compatibility workarounds with bug/reference and removal criteria.
- [`CSS-QUAL-0006`](#css-qual-0006) — Keep source maps and generated CSS out of handwritten source ownership.
- [`CSS-QUAL-0007`](#css-qual-0007) — Test themes, interaction states, long content, empty content, and zoom.
- [`CSS-QUAL-0008`](#css-qual-0008) — Use visual regression tests for high-value stable components where practical.
- [`CSS-QUAL-0009`](#css-qual-0009) — Review computed styles when debugging rather than adding speculative overrides.
- [`CSS-QUAL-0010`](#css-qual-0010) — Delete superseded compatibility rules promptly.

## Resolved Rules

### <a id="css-gen-0001"></a> CSS-GEN-0001 — Keep CSS in external stylesheet files.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `General → GEN → General → CSS-GEN-0001`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && General`

Keep CSS in external stylesheet files.

Rationale: HTML must remain free of style elements and style attributes; external CSS improves caching, CSP, tooling, and separation of concerns.

**Rationale:** HTML must remain free of style elements and style attributes; external CSS improves caching, CSP, tooling, and separation of concerns.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-gen-0002"></a> CSS-GEN-0002 — Use modern CSS directly when project browser support permits it.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `General → GEN → General → CSS-GEN-0002`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && General`

Use modern CSS directly when project browser support permits it.

Rationale: Avoid legacy workarounds and preprocess-style patterns when the platform provides the required primitive.

**Rationale:** Avoid legacy workarounds and preprocess-style patterns when the platform provides the required primitive.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `General → GEN → General → CSS-GEN-0003`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && General`

Prefer declarative CSS over JavaScript-driven presentation.

Rationale: Layout, responsive behavior, state styling, and animation should remain in CSS when they do not require application logic.

**Rationale:** Layout, responsive behavior, state styling, and animation should remain in CSS when they do not require application logic.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

**Priority:** `SHOULD`  
**Concept path:** `General → GEN → General → CSS-GEN-0004`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && General`

Use a deterministic formatter and consistent property ordering.

Rationale: Formatting policy should eliminate style-only review noise.

**Rationale:** Formatting policy should eliminate style-only review noise.

### <a id="css-gen-0005"></a> CSS-GEN-0005 — Remove dead declarations and selectors.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `General → GEN → General → CSS-GEN-0005`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && General`

Remove dead declarations and selectors.

Rationale: Unused CSS increases transfer, cascade complexity, and maintenance burden.

**Rationale:** Unused CSS increases transfer, cascade complexity, and maintenance burden.

### <a id="css-gen-0006"></a> CSS-GEN-0006 — Avoid !important.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `General → GEN → General → CSS-GEN-0006`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && General`

Avoid !important.

Rationale: Important declarations flatten the cascade and make overrides depend on escalating specificity.

**Example / guidance:**

```text
Use layers, source order, scope, or better ownership instead.
```

**Rationale:** Important declarations flatten the cascade and make overrides depend on escalating specificity.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

### <a id="css-gen-0007"></a> CSS-GEN-0007 — Prefer logical properties when layout should adapt to writing mode.

**Priority:** `SHOULD`  
**Concept path:** `General → GEN → General → CSS-GEN-0007`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && General`

Prefer logical properties when layout should adapt to writing mode.

Rationale: margin-inline, inset-block, and related properties encode intent instead of physical direction.

**Rationale:** margin-inline, inset-block, and related properties encode intent instead of physical direction.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

### <a id="css-gen-0008"></a> CSS-GEN-0008 — Use comments for non-obvious constraints and public styling APIs.

**Priority:** `SHOULD`  
**Concept path:** `General → GEN → General → CSS-GEN-0008`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && General`

Use comments for non-obvious constraints and public styling APIs.

Rationale: Comments should explain why, ownership, custom-property contracts, or browser constraints—not restate declarations.

**Rationale:** Comments should explain why, ownership, custom-property contracts, or browser constraints—not restate declarations.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

### <a id="css-gen-0009"></a> CSS-GEN-0009 — Do not create one-use custom properties that add indirection without semantic value.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `General → GEN → General → CSS-GEN-0009`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && General`

Do not create one-use custom properties that add indirection without semantic value.

Rationale: A token is useful when reused, externally configurable, calculated, or conceptually named; otherwise direct values are clearer.

**Rationale:** A token is useful when reused, externally configurable, calculated, or conceptually named; otherwise direct values are clearer.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

### <a id="css-gen-0010"></a> CSS-GEN-0010 — Keep source order intentional.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `General → GEN → General → CSS-GEN-0010`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && General`

Keep source order intentional.

Rationale: Source order is part of the cascade and should not be treated as accidental.

**Rationale:** Source order is part of the cascade and should not be treated as accidental.

### <a id="css-cas-0001"></a> CSS-CAS-0001 — Use cascade layers to express stylesheet precedence when multiple origins of project CSS compete.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Cascade & Specificity → CAS → Cascade & Specificity → CSS-CAS-0001`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Cascade & Specificity`

Use cascade layers to express stylesheet precedence when multiple origins of project CSS compete.

Rationale: @layer makes precedence explicit without specificity escalation.

**Example / guidance:**

```text
@layer reset, tokens, base, components, utilities, overrides;
```

**Rationale:** @layer makes precedence explicit without specificity escalation.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-cas-0002"></a> CSS-CAS-0002 — Keep component selectors low-specificity.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Cascade & Specificity → CAS → Cascade & Specificity → CSS-CAS-0002`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Cascade & Specificity`

Keep component selectors low-specificity.

Rationale: Low specificity makes states, themes, and composition easier to override predictably.

**Example / guidance:**

```text
Prefer .card-title over #app .page .card > h3.card-title.
```

**Rationale:** Low specificity makes states, themes, and composition easier to override predictably.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

**Applicability:** `Browser && Cascade & Specificity`

Avoid id selectors for styling.

Rationale: IDs carry excessive specificity and couple styling to unique document identity.

**Rationale:** IDs carry excessive specificity and couple styling to unique document identity.

Use :is() to group equivalent selector branches without duplication.

### <a id="css-cas-0008"></a> CSS-CAS-0008 — Do not rely on accidental stylesheet import order.

Do not rely on accidental stylesheet import order.

### <a id="css-cas-0010"></a> CSS-CAS-0010 — Scope exceptions narrowly.

Scope exceptions narrowly.

### <a id="css-sel-0001"></a> CSS-SEL-0001 — Name classes by semantic role or component responsibility.

Name classes by semantic role or component responsibility.

### <a id="css-sel-0002"></a> CSS-SEL-0002 — Use classes as the default styling hook.

### <a id="css-sel-0003"></a> CSS-SEL-0003 — Avoid styling behavior-only data attributes unless the state itself is part of the styling API.

Avoid styling behavior-only data attributes unless the state itself is part of the styling API.

### <a id="css-sel-0004"></a> CSS-SEL-0004 — Avoid deep descendant selectors.

### <a id="css-sel-0005"></a> CSS-SEL-0005 — Prefer direct child selectors when component structure is contractual.

### <a id="css-sel-0006"></a> CSS-SEL-0006 — Use attribute selectors for actual attribute semantics.

### <a id="css-sel-0008"></a> CSS-SEL-0008 — Use :has() only when the relationship itself is the styling condition.

### <a id="css-sel-0009"></a> CSS-SEL-0009 — Avoid universal-selector rules outside deliberate resets or scoped algorithms.

### <a id="css-tok-0003"></a> CSS-TOK-0003 — Separate global design tokens from component-local variables.

### <a id="css-tok-0004"></a> CSS-TOK-0004 — Provide defaults for externally overridable component custom properties when sensible.

**Applicability:** `Browser && Accessibility`

Do not reorder meaningful content solely with flex/grid order.

Rationale: Visual order that differs from DOM/focus order can confuse keyboard and screen-reader users.

**Rationale:** Visual order that differs from DOM/focus order can confuse keyboard and screen-reader users.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-a11y-0009"></a> CSS-A11Y-0009 — Support user color-scheme preferences only when both themes are complete.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Accessibility → A11Y → Accessibility → CSS-A11Y-0009`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Accessibility`

Support user color-scheme preferences only when both themes are complete.

Rationale: Partial dark/light modes can create unreadable controls or mismatched native surfaces.

**Rationale:** Partial dark/light modes can create unreadable controls or mismatched native surfaces.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-a11y-0010"></a> CSS-A11Y-0010 — Use motion, transparency, and contrast preferences as progressive user adaptations.

**Priority:** `SHOULD`  
**Concept path:** `Accessibility → A11Y → Accessibility → CSS-A11Y-0010`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Accessibility`

Use motion, transparency, and contrast preferences as progressive user adaptations.

Rationale: User preference media features should enhance accessibility without becoming required for basic usability.

**Rationale:** User preference media features should enhance accessibility without becoming required for basic usability.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-perf-0001"></a> CSS-PERF-0001 — Measure before applying performance-specific CSS complexity.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Performance & Rendering → PERF → Performance & Rendering → CSS-PERF-0001`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Performance & Rendering`

Measure before applying performance-specific CSS complexity.

Rationale: Optimization should address observed style/layout/paint/compositing cost rather than folklore.

**Rationale:** Optimization should address observed style/layout/paint/compositing cost rather than folklore.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-perf-0002"></a> CSS-PERF-0002 — Avoid selectors and rules that cause broad unnecessary invalidation in frequently mutating regions.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Performance & Rendering → PERF → Performance & Rendering → CSS-PERF-0002`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Performance & Rendering`

Avoid selectors and rules that cause broad unnecessary invalidation in frequently mutating regions.

Rationale: Dynamic DOM updates can make otherwise harmless selector relationships expensive.

**Rationale:** Dynamic DOM updates can make otherwise harmless selector relationships expensive.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-perf-0003"></a> CSS-PERF-0003 — Use contain when isolation semantics are correct.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Performance & Rendering → PERF → Performance & Rendering → CSS-PERF-0003`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Performance & Rendering`

Use contain when isolation semantics are correct.

Rationale: Containment can reduce layout/paint scope but changes sizing and rendering semantics.

**Rationale:** Containment can reduce layout/paint scope but changes sizing and rendering semantics.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-perf-0004"></a> CSS-PERF-0004 — Use content-visibility for large offscreen sections only when its accessibility and sizing behavior is understood.

**Priority:** `SHOULD`  
**Concept path:** `Performance & Rendering → PERF → Performance & Rendering → CSS-PERF-0004`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Performance & Rendering`

Use content-visibility for large offscreen sections only when its accessibility and sizing behavior is understood.

Rationale: Skipping rendering can reduce work but requires appropriate intrinsic-size handling.

**Rationale:** Skipping rendering can reduce work but requires appropriate intrinsic-size handling.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-perf-0005"></a> CSS-PERF-0005 — Avoid excessive box-shadow, filter, backdrop-filter, and large blur effects in animated surfaces.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Performance & Rendering → PERF → Performance & Rendering → CSS-PERF-0005`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Performance & Rendering`

Avoid excessive box-shadow, filter, backdrop-filter, and large blur effects in animated surfaces.

Rationale: Large filtered regions can be paint/GPU intensive.

**Rationale:** Large filtered regions can be paint/GPU intensive.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-perf-0006"></a> CSS-PERF-0006 — Do not add will-change permanently to many elements.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Performance & Rendering → PERF → Performance & Rendering → CSS-PERF-0006`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Performance & Rendering`

Do not add will-change permanently to many elements.

Rationale: will-change reserves optimization resources and can increase memory usage.

**Example / guidance:**

```text
Apply narrowly and preferably shortly before the change.
```

**Rationale:** will-change reserves optimization resources and can increase memory usage.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-perf-0007"></a> CSS-PERF-0007 — Minimize layout thrash by keeping measurement/mutation sequencing in JavaScript rather than trying to compensate with CSS hacks.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Performance & Rendering → PERF → Performance & Rendering → CSS-PERF-0007`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Performance & Rendering`

Minimize layout thrash by keeping measurement/mutation sequencing in JavaScript rather than trying to compensate with CSS hacks.

Rationale: CSS cannot repair repeated forced synchronous layout caused by script.

**Rationale:** CSS cannot repair repeated forced synchronous layout caused by script.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-perf-0008"></a> CSS-PERF-0008 — Reduce unused CSS delivered on critical routes.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Performance & Rendering → PERF → Performance & Rendering → CSS-PERF-0008`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Performance & Rendering`

Reduce unused CSS delivered on critical routes.

Rationale: Large stylesheets increase transfer and style processing even when many selectors never match.

**Rationale:** Large stylesheets increase transfer and style processing even when many selectors never match.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-perf-0009"></a> CSS-PERF-0009 — Prefer one coherent rule over many mutually overriding declarations.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Performance & Rendering → PERF → Performance & Rendering → CSS-PERF-0009`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Performance & Rendering`

Prefer one coherent rule over many mutually overriding declarations.

Rationale: Cascade churn increases style calculation complexity and human debugging cost.

**Rationale:** Cascade churn increases style calculation complexity and human debugging cost.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-perf-0010"></a> CSS-PERF-0010 — Treat expensive visual effects as responsive to device/user capability where appropriate.

**Priority:** `SHOULD`  
**Concept path:** `Performance & Rendering → PERF → Performance & Rendering → CSS-PERF-0010`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Performance & Rendering`

Treat expensive visual effects as responsive to device/user capability where appropriate.

Rationale: Low-power contexts may benefit from reduced effects.

**Rationale:** Low-power contexts may benefit from reduced effects.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-qual-0001"></a> CSS-QUAL-0001 — Run a CSS linter in CI.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Compatibility & Quality → QUAL → Compatibility & Quality → CSS-QUAL-0001`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Compatibility & Quality`

Run a CSS linter in CI.

Rationale: Static analysis catches invalid declarations, duplicate properties, unsupported syntax policies, and project conventions.

**Rationale:** Static analysis catches invalid declarations, duplicate properties, unsupported syntax policies, and project conventions.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-qual-0002"></a> CSS-QUAL-0002 — Test supported browser engines rather than relying on syntax compilation alone.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Compatibility & Quality → QUAL → Compatibility & Quality → CSS-QUAL-0002`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Compatibility & Quality`

Test supported browser engines rather than relying on syntax compilation alone.

Rationale: Parsing support does not guarantee identical layout, interaction, or rendering behavior.

**Rationale:** Parsing support does not guarantee identical layout, interaction, or rendering behavior.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-qual-0003"></a> CSS-QUAL-0003 — Use feature queries for optional enhancements when support varies across targets.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Compatibility & Quality → QUAL → Compatibility & Quality → CSS-QUAL-0003`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Compatibility & Quality`

Use feature queries for optional enhancements when support varies across targets.

Rationale: @supports allows progressive enhancement without user-agent detection.

**Rationale:** @supports allows progressive enhancement without user-agent detection.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-qual-0004"></a> CSS-QUAL-0004 — Avoid browser-targeted hacks unless a documented engine bug requires them.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Compatibility & Quality → QUAL → Compatibility & Quality → CSS-QUAL-0004`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Compatibility & Quality`

Avoid browser-targeted hacks unless a documented engine bug requires them.

Rationale: Hacks become stale and can affect future browser versions unexpectedly.

**Rationale:** Hacks become stale and can affect future browser versions unexpectedly.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-qual-0005"></a> CSS-QUAL-0005 — Document compatibility workarounds with bug/reference and removal criteria.

**Priority:** `SHOULD`  
**Concept path:** `Compatibility & Quality → QUAL → Compatibility & Quality → CSS-QUAL-0005`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Compatibility & Quality`

Document compatibility workarounds with bug/reference and removal criteria.

Rationale: A workaround should explain why it exists and when it can be deleted.

**Rationale:** A workaround should explain why it exists and when it can be deleted.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-qual-0006"></a> CSS-QUAL-0006 — Keep source maps and generated CSS out of handwritten source ownership.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Compatibility & Quality → QUAL → Compatibility & Quality → CSS-QUAL-0006`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Compatibility & Quality`

Keep source maps and generated CSS out of handwritten source ownership.

Rationale: Build artifacts should be reproducible and clearly separate from authored files.

**Rationale:** Build artifacts should be reproducible and clearly separate from authored files.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-qual-0007"></a> CSS-QUAL-0007 — Test themes, interaction states, long content, empty content, and zoom.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Compatibility & Quality → QUAL → Compatibility & Quality → CSS-QUAL-0007`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Compatibility & Quality`

Test themes, interaction states, long content, empty content, and zoom.

Rationale: Visual correctness requires state-space coverage beyond the default screenshot.

**Rationale:** Visual correctness requires state-space coverage beyond the default screenshot.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-qual-0008"></a> CSS-QUAL-0008 — Use visual regression tests for high-value stable components where practical.

**Priority:** `SHOULD`  
**Concept path:** `Compatibility & Quality → QUAL → Compatibility & Quality → CSS-QUAL-0008`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Compatibility & Quality`

Use visual regression tests for high-value stable components where practical.

Rationale: Screenshot comparisons can catch cascade/layout regressions not visible to unit tests.

**Rationale:** Screenshot comparisons can catch cascade/layout regressions not visible to unit tests.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-qual-0009"></a> CSS-QUAL-0009 — Review computed styles when debugging rather than adding speculative overrides.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Compatibility & Quality → QUAL → Compatibility & Quality → CSS-QUAL-0009`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Compatibility & Quality`

Review computed styles when debugging rather than adding speculative overrides.

Rationale: The cascade should be diagnosed from the winning declaration, specificity, layer, and inheritance chain.

**Rationale:** The cascade should be diagnosed from the winning declaration, specificity, layer, and inheritance chain.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

### <a id="css-qual-0010"></a> CSS-QUAL-0010 — Delete superseded compatibility rules promptly.

**Priority:** `MUST`  
**Concept path:** `Compatibility & Quality → QUAL → Compatibility & Quality → CSS-QUAL-0010`  
**Applicability:** `Browser && Compatibility & Quality`

Delete superseded compatibility rules promptly.

Rationale: Expired fallbacks create hidden branches in the styling system.

**Rationale:** Expired fallbacks create hidden branches in the styling system.

**Validation:** Run CSS validation, linting, and relevant browser tests.

---

## Glossary

- **MUST:** Mandatory requirement unless an explicit, justified exception is recorded.
- **SHOULD:** Strong recommendation; deviations require a concrete reason.
- **MAY:** Optional guidance whose applicability depends on context.
- **applicability:** The environments, runtimes, APIs, and scopes in which a rule is relevant.
- **autofix:** Whether a rule can be safely transformed automatically.
- **knowledge graph:** Rules plus inheritance bases and explicit typed relations.
